description: We are Team Carto Mars, a group of four students. We are eager to learn, curious about coding, and deeply fascinated by space. We are energetic people, ready to bring innovation.
summary:
Meridian 77 is an interactive 2D/3D Extravehicular Activity (EVA) route-planning and decision-support system
  designed for future astronauts exploring the Jezero Crater delta front on Mars.

  To address the challenge, Meridian 77 fuses eight co-registered NASA and USGS datasets—Mars 2020 1 m DEM topography,
  HiRISE/CTX optical imagery, USGS SIM 3464 geology, THEMIS thermal inertia, MEDA-calibrated surface temperature,
  CRISM 2.30 µm mineralogy, multi-sensor sand/dune detection, and MSL-RAD GCR/SEP radiation models. When crew members
  select any start and target coordinates, our explainable local Random Forest + Ridge ML ensemble (R² = 0.932, 5-fold
  CV R² = 0.942) dynamically adapts A* pathfinding weights to compare Shortest, Risk-Aware, and ML-Optimized traverses
  against a strict 6-hour life-support and turn-back budget.

  This is critical because human Mars exploration demands more than static maps: Meridian 77 transforms raw orbital
  and rover telemetry into transparent GO / CAUTION / NO-GO safety verdicts while maximizing scientific return.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

Meridian 77 is a local-first 2D/3D Extravehicular Activity (EVA) traverse planner and decision-support system for future astronauts operating across the Jezero Crater delta front on Mars (77.29°E–77.46°E, 18.39°N–18.56°N).

When a crew member selects a start station (such as Octavia E. Butler Landing) and a science target (such as Skinner Ridge or Upper Delta Margin) or clicks custom coordinates on the map, Meridian 77 samples the route every ~9 meters across eight co-registered NASA and USGS orbital/surface datasets:

• Topography & Slope: NASA Mars 2020 1 m DEM (9.77 m display grid) with 15° caution and 25° hard no-go slope thresholds, seamlessly blended with MGS MOLA in 3D view.

• Optical Imagery: 25 cm/px HiRISE and 6 m/px CTX orthorectified mosaic.

• Geology: USGS SIM 3464 1:75,000 geologic units (Jezero floor Njf, delta fan NHjf2, eolian bedforms Aeb).

• Thermal Inertia & Surface Temperature: Mars Odyssey THEMIS quantitative thermal inertia (SI) combined with DEM solar incidence and Perseverance MEDA TIRS ground temperature calibration (-40.0°C to -8.5°C).

• Mineralogy & Live Science Scoring: MRO CRISM (HRL000040FF) 2.30 µm Fe/Mg-phyllosilicate continuum-removed band depth sampled dynamically along the traverse, combined with Perseverance rover mineral assemblages.

• Aeolian Sand & Dune Detection: Multi-sensor classification combining HiRISE 25 cm ripple crest coherence, DEM slope masks, and THEMIS thermal inertia to flag active dunes and sand sheets.

• Ionizing Radiation & Horizon Shielding: Cumulative EVA dose calculator built on 40 quality-verified Curiosity RAD (MSL-M-RAD-3-RDR-V1.0) records for nominal GCR background (10.57 µGy/h) and the September 2017 GLE 72 Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) storm (21.63 µGy/h peak window), paired with an experimental 16-azimuth DEM sky-visibility (SVF) horizon model.

To optimize routes, Meridian 77 compares three candidate paths side-by-side: Route A (Shortest), Route B (Risk-Aware A*), and Route C (ML-Optimized). Route C is powered by a local, explainable 27-tree CART Random Forest (max_depth=13, 65% weight) + Ridge Regression (35% weight) ensemble trained on 850 unique Jezero corridors (Validation R² = 0.9320, Out-of-Bag R² = 0.9431, 5-Fold Spatial Cross-Validation R² = 0.9424 ± 0.0046, Y-Permutation Null R² = -0.1368 confirming zero data leakage).

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

Human exploration on Mars is strictly constrained by life-support consumables, terrain hazards, and turn-back deadlines. Meridian 77 converts complex multi-spectral orbital telemetry into an immediate, transparent GO / CAUTION / NO-GO verdict and a printable paper "Return-By Field Card."

It calculates exact outbound walk time (at 1.5 km/h on Mars's 3,389.5 km volumetric radius), science stop durations (20 min/stop), maximum safe target stay, and latest turn-back clock time within a 6-hour EVA budget (including a mandatory 30-minute reserve). Its intended impact is to bridge the gap between planetary science archives and operational astronaut safety—usable inside a habitat planning console, on a crew tablet, or printed as an emergency suit checklist.

3. How the Project Is Creative & Factors Considered

• Cartographic Traverse Sheet Design: Instead of a cluttered consumer dashboard, we designed Meridian 77 as a high-contrast tactical survey sheet with a synchronized 2D Leaflet map, a custom WebGL/Three.js 3D terrain engine with Web Worker mesh generation, and a printable field brief.

• Scientific Honesty & Uncertainty Handling: Rather than fabricating precision where orbital data is incomplete, our team explicitly modeled data limits: routes with >5% missing DEM coverage trigger an INSUFFICIENT DATA warning; Gale Crater RAD measurements are transparently labeled as regional environmental estimates transferred to Jezero; and geometric cliff shielding is never falsely equated to percentage GCR dose reduction due to secondary neutron scatter.

• Explainable AI (XAI) with Deterministic Safety Guardrails: Even when the ML ensemble predicts risk weights, a deterministic safety verifier checks every candidate route against hard physical constraints (>25° slope, active dune NO-GO rules, and 6-hour oxygen reserve). We also generated five publication-grade XAI diagnostic plots (MDI vs. Permutation Importance, Partial Dependence Curves, Local SHAP Waterfall, Parity/Residuals, and 5-Fold CV Audit).

4. Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

• Frontend & 3D Visualization: TypeScript, React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet (CRS.Simple planetary projection), Three.js / React Three Fiber (64-tile 3D terrain mesh & Web Workers), Zustand, and Recharts.

• Data Pipeline & Machine Learning: Python 3, NumPy, Pillow, Matplotlib (for raster warping, CRISM continuum removal, 16-azimuth horizon raycasting, Random Forest + Ridge training, and 300 DPI XAI charts).

• Verification & Testing: Vitest (109 passing unit tests covering geodesy, DEM sampling, EVA scoring, radiation physics, ML schema validation, data leakage, and overfitting audits) and Playwright end-to-end browser tests.
